title: Sulfur's Role in Organisms and Pathogenesis
summary: This cluster revolves around the importance of sulfur in various organisms and its involvement in pathogenic processes. Candida albicans and Cryptococcus neoformans are linked to sulfur amino acid biosynthetic pathways, while Aspergillus fumigatus is connected to this pathway as well. Sulfur metabolism and assimilation are crucial for the production of methionine synthase, which is utilized by Candida albicans. Hydrogen sulfide accumulation is associated with Sonal et al., and its growth is mediated by met17 deletion. Sulfur is vital to all organisms and is involved in the production of glutathione, which is utilized by Francisella. Oxidative stress and apoptosis are related to each other, and sulfur metabolism is involved in fungal pathogenesis.
